name: Klamath Basin Forests and Watersheds Restoration
summary: Request for proposals from NFWF and USDA NRCS for forest, watershed and fish and wildlife habitat restoration and monitoring across the Klamath Basin in Oregon and California.

amount.note: Shasta Valley RCPP track; the Upper Klamath Watershed Resilience track has a $100,000-$500,000 range

steps: Contact the NFWF programme manager before applying (Shasta Valley RCPP)

eligibility.rule: No international organisation, business, unincorporated individual or US federal agency.
Shasta RCPP: Shasta River watershed. Upper Klamath Resilience: Upper Klamath Basin in Oregon.
Keep Shasta project work outside the Shasta River Safe Harbor Agreement project list
Include an implementation component in a Shasta Valley RCPP project
Pair Shasta water-conservation projects with formal instream-flow protections
Shasta Valley RCPP: identify NRCS practices and keep costs within NRCS reimbursement rates
Shasta Valley RCPP work must meet the NRCS California Field Office Technical Guide specifications.

co_finance.applies_to: Upper Klamath (non-federal); Shasta Valley RCPP requires a 1:1 contribution

documents: NRCS Budget Template, completed for Shasta Valley RCPP, blank for the other funds
Statement of Litigation, except for federal, state and local governments
Board member list, or a no-board statement for non-nonprofits without a board
If no Single Audit, GAAP audit or applicable unaudited financial statements, unless current records are on file
IRS Form 990 or e-Postcard if applicable, or required substitute, unless current records are on file
Single Audit or signed exemption memo, unless current records are on file

status.quote: Full Proposal Due Date February 9, 2027, by 8:59 PM PST

deadline.quote: Full Proposal Due Date February 9, 2027, by 8:59 PM PST

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include: non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, special districts (e.g., conservation districts, planning districts, utility districts), and educational institutions.

geography.quote: fish and wildlife conservation, restoration, and monitoring projects across the Klamath Basin

access.quote: All application materials must be submitted online through National Fish and Wildlife Foundation's Easygrants system.

co_finance_required.quote: Klamath Basin Restoration Program projects are not required to provide cash or in-kind matching contributions. Shasta Valley RCPP projects must have a minimum cash or in-kind contribution of 100% (i.e., 1:1). Upper Klamath Watershed Resilience projects must have a minimum match of 25% non-federal cash or in-kind contributions.

effort.quote: All applicants to the Shasta Valley RCPP must contact NFWF Program Manager Erica Engstrom-Schau (erica.engstrom-schau@nfwf.org, 415-490-5211) prior to proposal submission to discuss their project and review required supplemental budget and technical materials.
Full Proposal Due Date February 9, 2027, by 8:59 PM PST

eligibility.quote: Ineligible applicants include: international organizations, businesses, unincorporated individuals, or U.S. Federal government agencies.

Projects must be located within the Shasta River watershed including Big Springs Creek, Parks Creek, or other tributaries. Figure 3. Target geography for Shasta Valley RCPP funding For Upper Klamath Watershed Resilience (NRCS): Projects must be located within the Upper Klamath Basin in Oregon
Due to federal environmental compliance considerations, proposed project work must not be included within the Shasta River Safe Harbor Agreement project list.
Proposed projects must include an implementation component.

All funded water conservation projects under this program must be paired with formal measures to protect instream flows such as a state-approved instream flow dedication or signed forbearance agreement.
Applicants must identify the NRCS Conservation Practice(s) and Scenario(s) to be supported by their proposed project and confirm that their project costs will align with NRCS reimbursement rates.

Eligible applicants include: non-profit 501(c) organizations, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, Tribal governments and organizations, special districts (e.g., conservation districts, planning districts, utility districts), and educational institutions.
Project types that will be eligible for funding must be aligned with, and meet the specifications of, the NRCS California Field Office Technical Guide.

co_finance.quote: Shasta Valley RCPP projects must have a minimum cash or in-kind contribution of 100% (i.e., 1:1). Upper Klamath Watershed Resilience projects must have a minimum match of 25% non-federal cash or in-kind contributions.

documents.quote: Applicants for Shasta Valley Regional Conservation Partnership Program funding must complete and upload the NRCS Budget Template.
Applicants for Klamath Basin Restoration Program funding or Upper Klamath Watershed Resilience funding must upload a blank version of the NRCS Budget Template.

Statement of Litigation Yes Template provided in Easygrants online application "Uploads" section. Federal, state, and local government applicants are not required to complete this section. Board of Trustees or Directors Yes Provide a list of members. If your organization is not a nonprofit and does not have a Board, upload a document stating that none exists. GAAP Audited Financial Statements*

IRS Form 990* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. Single Audit* Yes Please refer to the Required Financial Documents and FAQs webpage for details on all financial information required for submission. Applicant Controls Questionnaire Yes

If your organization does not meet the Single Audit threshold, please provide the applicable financial documentation in accordance with your organization’s policies and procedures. This may include GAAP-audited financial statements or, if a GAAP audited report is not applicable, a balance sheet and/or income statement, as appropriate.

If the entity is not required to file an IRS Form 990, they must provide a memo on company letterhead, signed with functional title, date and reason. If the entity is newly incorporated and has not filed the IRS Form 990, they must provide the entity’s IRS Tax Exempt Status Determination Letter.
